name: Preparing for a Full Kitchen Renovation: What to Do Before Demo Day

step.name: Step 1: Finalize Your Design and Selections — What to do: Ensure all design plans, including layouts, cabinetry, appliances, countertops, backsplash tile, flooring, and lighting, are fully approved and ordered. What to have ready: Signed contracts for all materials and a clear understanding of lead times. What done looks like: All major selections are made, confirmed, and on order, minimizing on-site decision-making.

What to have ready: Signed contracts for all materials and a clear understanding of lead times. What done looks like: All major selections are made, confirmed, and on order, minimizing on-site decision-making.

step.name: Step 2: Secure Necessary Permits — What to do: Coordinate with your design-build team, like AKN Design Group, to ensure all required permits for structural changes, plumbing, gas lines, or electrical work are obtained from the local building department. What to have ready: Approved design plans and documentation for permit applications. What done looks like: All necessary permits are issued and ready to be displayed on-site before construction begins, avoiding any regulatory stoppages.

step.name: Step 3: Plan for a Temporary Kitchen — What to do: Set up an alternate cooking and food prep area in your home, utilizing appliances like a microwave, toaster oven, or electric griddle. What to have ready: A designated space, basic cooking appliances, and essential dishware. What done looks like: You have a functional setup that minimizes disruption to your daily routine during the weeks or months your main kitchen is out of commission.

step.name: Step 4: Protect Your Home and Belongings — What to do: Clear out all items from the kitchen, remove wall hangings from adjacent rooms, and ensure pathways for workers are clear. Cover furniture and flooring in nearby areas to protect against dust and debris. What to have ready: Storage for kitchen contents and protective coverings. What done looks like: Your home is shielded from construction dust and potential damage, ensuring a cleaner and safer work environment.

step.name: Step 5: Confirm Project Schedule and Communication — What to do: Review the detailed project timeline with your contractor, understanding key milestones, expected completion dates, and communication protocols. What to have ready: A clear understanding of the schedule and contact information for your project manager. What done looks like: You're aligned with your team on expectations, ensuring clear communication throughout the renovation journey.
